title: Any-true machine run
statement: Let $x$ and $r$ be Boolean words, and write $x=p r$ for a split into a prefix $p$ and suffix $r$. There is a time $t \le |r|+1$ such that the designated any-true machine, started in its scanning state with input head just past $p$ and empty output, is halted and has output consisting of the single bit that is true exactly when $r$ contains a true bit.
hypotheses_covered: A prefix p with x = p ++ r
caveat: The statement's machine f2_anyTrueTM is not defined among the supplied definitions; the output behavior is clear from the claim, but the machine's identity is not.
